task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of normal, unexpanded portal tracts with sharp boundaries, showing clear separation from the surrounding hepatic parenchyma and an absence of dense cellular clustering.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of well-defined, continuous, and regular tubular or circular outlines of interlobular bile ducts lacking any architectural distortion.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of smooth, distinct luminal boundaries of central veins and interlobular vessels, surrounded by uniform and structurally normal hepatic lobular architecture.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a minority of portal tracts showing patchy, sparse regions of increased cellularity, while maintaining normal overall size without significant structural expansion.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of largely intact overall architecture in interlobular bile ducts, but with a minority showing subtle, focal thickening or slight irregularity along the ductal outline.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of subtle, focal irregularities in the luminal contours of a minority of interlobular vessels or central veins, without observable alteration to the surrounding parenchyma.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of noticeable widening and structural expansion in the majority or all portal tracts, presenting as densified stromal areas with generally defined borders confined to the portal regions.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of widespread structural irregularity in the majority of interlobular bile ducts, exhibiting visually heterogeneous epithelial borders and noticeable ductal distortion.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of noticeable luminal contour irregularities across the majority or all interlobular vessels and central veins, accompanied by focal, limited patches of architectural clearing in the immediate perivenular regions.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of markedly widened portal tracts with dense, prominent cellularity and irregular, blurred boundaries indicating macroscopic structural spillover into the adjacent periportal hepatic tissue.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe architectural distortion, presenting as fragmented, collapsed, or ill-defined ductal remnants indicating widespread degeneration in the majority of bile ducts.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe architectural disruption around central veins, featuring expanded inflammatory halos that extend outward into the lobule, causing macroscopic perivenular tissue degradation.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of normal portal stroma lacking inflammatory cell infiltration, featuring native connective tissue and unremarkable vascular and biliary structures.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of an intact single layer of biliary epithelium featuring uniform nuclei, regular basal polarity, and a complete absence of intraepithelial inflammatory cells.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a flat, continuous endothelial cell monolayer without any subendothelial lifting, expansion, or attached inflammatory cells.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of sparse infiltration of predominantly mononuclear inflammatory cells, such as lymphocytes, localized within the portal stroma without notable edema.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of occasional intraepithelial inflammatory cells penetrating the ductal wall, accompanied by mild epithelial injury shown as slightly enlarged nuclei and an increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of sparse subendothelial infiltration of inflammatory cells in a minority of vessels, causing localized, mild lifting and separation of the endothelial cells from the underlying basement membrane.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of mixed inflammatory cell infiltration including lymphocytes, plasma cells, and occasional neutrophils or eosinophils, accompanied by visible portal edema and swollen microvascular endothelial cells.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of abundant intraepithelial inflammatory cell infiltration causing marked biliary epithelial damage, characterized by prominent nuclear pleomorphism, loss of cellular polarity, and cytoplasmic vacuolization.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of widespread subendothelial inflammatory infiltrates causing pronounced endothelial lifting, alongside a minority of perivenular hepatocyte dropout characterized by localized cell loss.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe portal edema and dense mixed inflammatory infiltrates extending beyond the limiting plate, directly intermingling with and disrupting the adjacent periportal hepatocytes.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe degenerative changes, including focal areas of ductal lumen disruption and structural breakdown, mixed with necrotic cellular debris and intense intraepithelial inflammation.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of moderate to severe central venulitis and perivenulitis with dense inflammatory infiltrates, resulting in extensive necrosis, fragmentation, and collapse of the surrounding perivenular hepatocytes.
